highlights: The hub is where every agent arrives and reports: Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex CLI and the Codex app connect through the cchub MCP server (Settings › Connections)
Delegate work into a workspace from any agent; runs start in the workspace context with every repo attached, show up as regular sessions, and can be followed, steered or cancelled
When a repo is busy, a delegated task moves to its own git worktree automatically, gets a reserved port block for dev servers, and keeps off files that interactive sessions have claimed
Workspaces come from your .code-workspace folder: list, create, edit, open, and install the wk alias for bash or PowerShell
Flow: workspaces, sessions, subagents and delegated tasks as one live map
Sessions shows Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex CLI and Codex app threads with running subagents and favorites, and a runtime bar of everything running on the machine

Usage (opt-in): what burns tokens per day, project, session and model, split into cache reads, fresh input and output, with context-per-message stats; read from local transcripts and cached between restarts
Limits (opt-in): Claude 5-hour, weekly and per-model limits and Codex 5-hour and weekly windows, account-wide, read-only, refreshed at the interval you pick
The widget docks to the left, right or top edge as a small tab with weekly-limit rings for Claude and Codex; open it for sessions (needs you, running, idle, delegated) or usage
Daily (opt-in): a guided daily note in your Markdown or Obsidian vault (close yesterday, confirm today, compose from your template) with an indentation-true preview, task filters and two-way sync
Session trail (opt-in): the hub summarizes each session into key points in your second brain, light, medium or high detail, and agent reports land in the same day file

Share: a link (on the LAN, or public through an ngrok tunnel the hub starts and installs itself) that lets another person and their assistant ask your Claude read-only questions about a workspace, or delegate work into it, with a key per link, expiry, rate limit, pause/revoke and a log of every question and answer
Trust levels on shares: Low (read-only, plans), Medium (edits, no shell), High (edits + safe shell), Total (no blocks); every level can ask, delegate and follow tasks
Persistent forks on shares: each asker keeps a live Claude session that remembers the conversation; askers identify themselves, answers can stream, and files travel both ways
Per-event desktop notifications in the hub's own toast window, with Windows toasts optional
Delegated runs are autonomous by default (bypass permissions / sandbox), and Settings › General can start the app with Windows
Dracula theme (VS Code / Obsidian palette) with the previous Midnight look still available in Settings › Appearance
Fixes: no more freeze at startup when ngrok is a Microsoft Store alias, and plan limits work behind antivirus TLS inspection by trusting the system certificates
Version chip and what's-new changelog in the hub
Landing page shows the current version and latest release notes
Release script now requires a changelog entry and ships a versioned installer
Headless sessions (SDK / claude -p) no longer enter the hub
Empty sessions are purged automatically after 12h (HUB_EMPTY_TTL_HOURS)
Session groups can be collapsed, with a needs-attention counter when closed
HUB_SKIP environment variable makes notify hooks exit early
Mobile LAN access with PWA manifest, title badge and vibration
Release script and containerization (Dockerfile)
First public release: session board, notifications, always-on-top widget, VS Code focus, WSL support and .msi installer
